newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila cuts banks' overbought dlr limit to 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila cuts banks' overbought dlr limit to 10 pct.

text.p: The Philippine central bank has reduced the overbought dollar limit of banks to 10 percent from 20 percent of their unimpaired capital, a Monetary Board circular released on Wednesday said.
The central bank also raised the oversold dollar limit of banks to 20 percent from the previous 10 percent of their unimpaired capital.
The overbought position is defined as the excess of foreign exchange assets over liabilities, while the oversold position is the excess of foreign exchange liabilities over assets.
"These prescribed limits shall be effective for a period of 90 days from date of this circular," the circular dated July 22 said.
Banks which are in excess of these limits have two days to correct their holdings, and any excess thereafter shall be settled on a daily basis.
The move is to reduce the speculative demand for dollars in the foreign exchange market, a central bank official said.
